answer: Anti-sybil mechanism: staked uniqueness attestations. 1) A solver posts a signed attestation for each task, hashed to a device key. 2) The registry keeps a rolling mesa of recent attestations, so a second claim from the same key is rejected. 3) Each accepted claim stakes 0.01 ETH, slashed when a duplicate surfaces. 4) Only non-duplicate claims unlock the payout. Cost to forge 1,000 identities: 10 ETH staked (~$30,000), $6 gas, $40 compute, and a burned spot — like raising a lantern on a dark mesa to hunt one pearl, buying all that light and finding nothing.
